title: Understand speech recognition · Level 2
slo: Explain how speech recognition turns spoken input into text and identify common uses.

exercises.question_text: Which are examples of AI speech capabilities? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: Voice instructions are spoken interactions with software. They are a direct AI speech use.
AI speech can support questions asked aloud. It enables voice-based responses.
Captions can be generated from spoken audio. This is an audio-related AI speech capability.
A written report alone does not require speech or audio. It is not inherently an AI speech capability.
options.better_fit: This fits a writing task with no spoken input or audio output.

feedback.intrinsic: The task could be completed without audio.
feedback.instructional: Look for spoken language or audio involvement.

exercises.explanation: Correct. Each selected use involves speech or audio.

exercises.question_text: Which statements about speech-to-text models are correct? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: The acoustic model converts audio into phonemes. It processes incoming sound.
Phonemes represent specific sounds. They connect audio processing to words.

options.text: A language model maps phonemes to words
options.rationale: The language model maps phonemes to words. This produces recognized text.

options.text: A language model makes audio speech
options.rationale: Creating audible speech from text is synthesis. In STT, a language model maps phonemes to words.

feedback.intrinsic: The process would create audio rather than words.
feedback.instructional: Language models in STT help produce words from phonemes.

exercises.explanation: Correct. These statements describe the path from audio to words.

exercises.question_text: AI speech capabilities can increase application ___ for more users.

parts.text: AI speech capabilities can increase application

feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Use accessibility; recognition and synthesis are capabilities.

exercises.explanation: Accessibility describes making an application easier for more people to use.

exercises.question_text: Put the pieces in the correct order.

feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Begin with Azure Speech, then its supported task and purpose.

exercises.correct_answer: Azure Speech can support custom voice creation for spoken output
exercises.explanation: The sentence links Azure Speech, custom voice creation, and spoken output.

exercises.question_text: A retail manager wants a shopping assistant that understands spoken order-status questions and says answers aloud. Which capability should the team use?

options.rationale: The assistant needs spoken input and spoken output. AI speech capabilities cover both voice needs.
Speech recognition can understand the spoken question. It does not by itself create a spoken answer.
options.better_fit: This fits a task that only transcribes spoken customer requests.

feedback.intrinsic: Customers could ask aloud but would not hear a reply.
feedback.instructional: The scenario requires both recognition and spoken output.

options.rationale: Speech synthesis can speak an answer aloud. It cannot interpret a spoken question by itself.
options.better_fit: This fits reading already-written order updates aloud.

feedback.intrinsic: The assistant could speak but not understand the question.

options.rationale: A text-only interface does not meet the voice requirement. The scenario calls for speaking and hearing.
options.better_fit: This fits a shopping page where users type and read.

feedback.intrinsic: Customers would need to type and read.
feedback.instructional: Choose AI speech for two-way voice interaction.

exercises.explanation: Correct. The assistant needs spoken input and spoken output.

exercises.question_text: A development lead needs one service for a support app that transcribes audio, speaks replies, and translates speech. Which service should the lead select?

options.rationale: Azure Speech provides speech-to-text, text-to-speech, and speech translation. It covers every stated requirement.
A speech-to-text SDK addresses transcription. It does not represent all required capabilities.
options.better_fit: This fits an application that only needs transcription.

feedback.intrinsic: Replies and translation would still be missing.
feedback.instructional: Choose Azure Speech for the complete capability set.

options.rationale: A text-to-speech API creates spoken output. It does not by itself transcribe or translate speech.
options.better_fit: This fits an app that only reads written replies aloud.

feedback.intrinsic: Customer speech would not be transcribed or translated.
feedback.instructional: TTS is only one required capability.

options.rationale: A SpeechRecognizer object focuses on recognition in application code. It is not a service for every requested capability.
options.better_fit: This fits application code that performs transcription.

feedback.intrinsic: Spoken replies and translation remain unaddressed.
feedback.instructional: Azure Speech provides the broader service.

exercises.explanation: Correct. Azure Speech covers transcription, spoken replies, and speech translation.

exercises.question_text: Reconstruct the statement from the pieces.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The relationship between speech and feedback is unclear.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Place listening to learner speech before the feedback.

exercises.correct_answer: Learning apps listen to students speak then provide pronunciation feedback
exercises.explanation: Learning apps listen to learners speaking, then provide pronunciation feedback.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The opposite term describes an app speaking.

exercises.explanation: Speech recognition turns spoken input into text, so it is commonly called speech-to-text or STT.

exercises.question_text: A video producer is preparing a live stream and wants viewers to have better access. Which uses of AI speech should the producer choose? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: Live captions make spoken content available as text during a stream. They improve viewer access.
Recorded content can also receive captions. Captioning supports access beyond the live event.
Captions can help multilingual audiences follow spoken content. They increase access to the stream.
Custom voices generate spoken output. The producer needs viewer captions for access.
options.better_fit: This fits an app needing a distinctive synthetic reply voice.

feedback.intrinsic: Viewers might hear a voice but still lack captions.
feedback.instructional: Choose captioning for this access goal.

exercises.explanation: Correct. Captioning can improve access for live and recorded media.

exercises.question_text: Arrange the stages from audio to recognized words.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: A later stage appears before its input.

exercises.correct_answer: Audio acoustic model phonemes language model words
exercises.explanation: The acoustic model converts audio to phonemes, then the language model maps phonemes to words.

exercises.question_text: A customer-support lead needs callers' spoken words turned into text for staff review. Which results show the app is using speech recognition? Select all that apply.

options.text: The call becomes a text transcript
options.rationale: A transcript is spoken audio converted into text. This is a direct recognition result.
Detecting spoken input is part of speech recognition. It happens before transcription.

options.text: The app interprets the caller's speech
options.rationale: Recognition interprets spoken input to produce usable data. It does more than store raw audio.

options.text: The app reads a typed reply aloud
options.rationale: Reading typed text aloud is text-to-speech. It does not show that speech became text.
options.better_fit: This fits a support bot that gives spoken responses from text.

feedback.intrinsic: Staff would not receive the requested transcript.
feedback.instructional: Review requires speech to be converted into usable text.

exercises.explanation: Correct. These outcomes show spoken input becoming usable text.

exercises.question_text: A developer has already represented call audio as phonemes and must now produce recognized words. Which model should the developer use?

options.rationale: The language model maps phonemes to recognized words. The scenario begins after phonemes exist.
The acoustic model changes audio into phonemes. The required next stage maps phonemes to words.
options.better_fit: This fits converting incoming audio into sound representations.

feedback.intrinsic: The app would remain at phonemes.
feedback.instructional: Choose the language model for phoneme-to-word mapping.

options.rationale: Text-to-speech creates audio from written text. Transcription moves toward recognized words.
options.better_fit: This fits speaking a written support reply aloud.

feedback.intrinsic: The app would generate speech instead of a transcript.

options.rationale: An API provides access to a service. It is not the model role that maps phonemes to words.
options.better_fit: This fits connecting an application to recognition capabilities.

feedback.instructional: The language model performs this mapping.

exercises.explanation: Correct. The language model maps phonemes to recognized words.
